result.defense: C is the only proposal meeting all criteria: it draws the founder's two interactive poses once — inner Inbox message in 1/3+2/3 split so Archive, Reply, More (Cleanup) and Ask Inbox agent can be checked against the x435-455 fold, and laptop Computer with keyboard below the y435-455 fold, key bar, and Release occupying the exact Take control slot — fixes the Desk rule/board mismatch, and assigns every undrawn page a named template via the coverage table without redrawing decisions. A fails criterion 1 outright and substitutes a vague 'derive from rule card' note for template assignment, leaving keyboard occlusion and fold placement untested. B draws the message in the wrong half-folded pose already covered by Inner, and wastes four boards duplicating Split (Finance/Legal inner) and Desk (Data room laptop), creating five 626x890/890x626 surfaces to keep in sync while Finance, Inbox and Computer copy are still changing; its one correct board, Computer laptop, is already in C. No graft: C already incorporates A's Inner chip and Desk fix, and any B board would violate the no-duplication criterion.

Proposal C is the only option that satisfies all four acceptance criteria while respecting cross-cluster maintenance constraints. It draws the exact two high-interaction boards required by the persona and Criterion 1 (Inbox message on the inner display with Archive, Reply, More/Cleanup, and Ask Inbox agent; Computer in laptop pose with the system keyboard, key bar, and Release in the Take control slot), aligns the Desk rule card with the Desk board (Criterion 2), maps all undrawn pages to explicit native split-view templates in a coverage table (Criterion 3), and avoids duplicating layouts across clusters (Criterion 4). Proposal A is rejected because it fails Criterion 1 by adding no boards at all, leaving the core persona interactions unillustrated. Proposal B is rejected because drawing five boards—including Finance inner, Legal inner, and Data room laptop—Directly violates Criterion 4 by duplicating standard list-plus-detail patterns and creating severe synchronization risk with clusters actively editing Finance data and copy.
